To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the maximum efficiency of a two-transmitter-two-receiver inductive power transfer (IPT) system with cross-coupling between the transmitters and between the receivers can be derived by jointly optimizing input and output currents; and (b) the maximum efficiency is determined by the system kQ-product.

the maximum efficiency of inductive wireless power transfer system with multiple transmitters and receivers can be formulated in terms of system kQ-products, and system kQ-products can be approximated by the sum of individual kQ-products.
the maximum RF-to RF efficiency of inductive coupling system with two transitters and two receivers can be expressed as a system kQ product.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the kQ-product analysis of an IPT system with multiple transmitters and receivers.
the kQ-product analysis of a multi-transmitter-multi-receiver inductive power transfer systems, which provides useful insight into the design of multi-link inductive power transfer.
inductive power transfer systems that are composed of two transmitters and/or two receivers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the maximum efficiency of a system with two transceivers is equal to the square root of the sum of square root of the efficiency of each individual transmitter-receiver link.
the kQ-product is an important parameter to characterize the efficiency of the IPT system.
the kQ-product of a system is the product of kQ-product of its individual links, and it is the kQ-product that determines the maximum efficiency of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the kQ-product analysis provides a simple and intuitive approach to the maximum efficiency of inductive coupling power transfer systems.
we have formulated a new concept, the system kQ-product and its relation to the maximum efficiency.
, for the system with two transmitter and two receivers, the square of the maximum efficiency can be approximated by sum of the square of the individual transmitter-receiver link efficiencies.

the system kQ-product is an important parameter to characterize the efficiency of inductive wireless power transfer system.
the kQ-product is the key parameter to evaluate the efficiency of a multi-transmitter and multi-receiver system.
